--font-body.value:
var(--font-plex-thai), 'IBM Plex Sans Thai', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'Segoe UI',
    'Noto Sans SC', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

decisions.decision: The manager appointment control uses the portal's existing staff form, card, button, and brand-token patterns in a responsive 42-cell month calendar with no time slots.
decisions.reason: The 21st.dev catalog search was unavailable (HTTP 401); the existing primitives satisfy the required accessibility, responsive behavior, and visual consistency.

decisions.decision: The learner name-card preview uses a proof-sheet layout: enlarged front and back pages side by side on desktop and stacked on mobile, with explicit side labels.
decisions.reason: Showing both sides removes PDF paging ambiguity and improves legibility. The 21st.dev catalog search was unavailable (HTTP 401), so the layout follows the portal's existing brand tokens and card primitives.

decisions.decision: The learner dashboard is task-first on phones: a compact identity header, four-step progress strip, four direct action cards, and an essential company summary; the richer desktop view remains intact.
decisions.reason: Learners primarily use phones. Short labels and full-card tap targets reduce reading and navigation effort, while manager-owned appointment booking is removed from learner actions. The 21st.dev catalog search was unavailable (HTTP 401), so the selected screenshots and existing portal tokens guided the implementation.

decisions.decision: The modern task-first learner dashboard is preserved, while the company section becomes a vertically scrollable set of complete DBD fact cards on mobile.
decisions.reason: The phone viewport can scroll, and learners need the complete company record for study. Website and Facebook cards are conditional so absent links do not leave empty rows or icons.

decisions.decision: The learner dashboard contains four learner-owned stages only: study, name card, quiz, and readiness interview. Bank appointment is absent from learner progress and actions at every breakpoint.
decisions.reason: Appointment booking is manager-owned. Removing it from learner navigation prevents a misleading fifth step while preserving the manager workflow and the learner's read-only appointment route.

decisions.decision: The learner study overview uses a progress-first mobile composition with four fixed-width stage tabs and compact lesson rows containing short localized titles, completion state, and a review or continue action.
decisions.reason: The user selected this supplied visual direction exactly. It removes the back control and horizontally scrolling stage strip, keeps all navigation visible without sideways scrolling, and puts course completion at the top.

decisions.decision: The readiness home leads with a compact four-point guide and a visible 9/11 target; the result shows the learner's score and only the answers that need more practice.
decisions.reason: The readiness flow should motivate rather than intimidate. The 21st.dev catalog search was unavailable (HTTP 401), so the implementation reuses the portal's responsive cards, semantic brand tokens, and mobile-first spacing.
